_generated: 2026-08-31 — measured against the live store, one source at a time
_what: THE IDENTITY RULE OF EVERY UPLOADED SOURCE: the fields that make one row one fact. Ingest keeps ONE row per key; a later upload of the same key supersedes the earlier row instead of stacking beside it. This file is the record; each app inlines an operative copy as SOURCE_KEYS because both must run from file://, and diagnostics/verify-source-keys.mjs fails on drift between the three.
_why: The rule already existed in three places and ran in one. migration-010-source-tables.sql encodes it as a PRIMARY KEY per table (eight of those tables have never received a row), PULSE states ViciDial's as `recordKey`, and the Ops upload station applies a supersede branch to exactly three sources. Everything else appended whatever arrived: the closed-case store held the same export seven times, 141 535 rows carrying 35 463 cases.
_measure_before_you_key: EVERY KEY HERE WAS COUNTED AGAINST THE LIVE DATA, AND TWO OF THEM WERE WRONG UNTIL IT WAS. bi_active_cases dropped R128.69 of real premium before its key gained contract_number and charge_code (restored from backup within the minute); vici_call_report would have deleted 2 016 real calls had it been keyed on the day rather than the timestamp. A key is a claim about the world. Test it against the world, and read what you are about to delete BEFORE you delete it — rows that arrive together in one batch are distinct facts, not a re-upload.

AGENT_LIST.sql: agent_list (as_of, employee_code) — the table keeps every dated snapshot; the blob holds only the current one
AGENT_LIST.note: One row per agent. Measured, not assumed: the blob carries _d as null on every roster row (the list is a live snapshot the app replaces wholesale), so a date component keys nothing at all — keyed on (_d, cb_norm) all 123 rows came back unkeyable. The dated history lives in the agent_list TABLE, keyed (as_of, employee_code); this key is the blob's.

ATTENDANCE.note: New file wins per employee-day — a month-to-date export followed by the full month must never double-count a day into the attendance denominators. Already enforced at ingest before this file existed.

BI_ACTIVE_CASES.note: THE KEY THAT WAS WRONG, AND THE MONEY PROVED IT. Keyed on (case, account, charge, date) the backfill dropped 4 rows and R128.69 of REAL premium: case 21217153 carries three separate contracts at the same charge amount, and case 21194675 carries Homedrive R49 beside MyPanic Single R49 — two products, one price, one day. All four pairs arrived in ONE batch (B0065), which is the tell: rows that appear together in a single file are distinct facts, not a re-upload. The money model is Sum of Charge Amount per account, so every contract line is its own fact and contract_number plus charge_code belong in the key. Restored from backup the same minute; the store is back at 13 434 rows and R398 414.86.

measured.note: zero duplicates on the corrected key — the 4 the coarse key found were legitimate contract lines

QA_EVALUATIONS.note: The Hub's own record id. A re-issued evaluation carries the same id and must replace, not join, its earlier copy.

SF_OPEN_CASES.note: A snapshot source: the lead book as at a moment. The station already replaces it wholesale, and it refuses an empty file so a frameset shell cannot wipe the book.

SF_CLOSED_CASES.note: A case closes once, so the case number IS the fact. Keyed on (case_number, closed_at) the count is the same to within one row — but a case whose closed_at is corrected by a later export would then keep BOTH rows, so the case number alone is the safer key. Later export wins: it carries the current status, disposition and age.

measured.note: seven copies of one export — batches B0043-B0048 and B0071 are each exactly 17 446 rows

SF_INACTIVE.note: Cancellations — the source that decides which sales are counted net. 394 of the 400 duplicates are byte-identical rows; the remaining 6 differ only in fields the later export refreshes.

VICI_CALL_REPORT.sql: vici_calls (call_date, agent_login, lead_id, status) — call_date is a TIMESTAMPTZ, so the SQL key is correct
VICI_CALL_REPORT.note: THE KEY THAT NEARLY CHANGED. Keyed on the full timestamp every one of the 29 315 live rows is distinct and there is nothing to dedupe. Keyed on the DAY — which is how the blob's own _d field and PULSE's recordKey label both read at a glance — 2 016 rows collapse, and they are not duplicates: an agent ringing the same lead twice in a day with the same disposition made two calls, each with its own length_in_sec. Talk time is the SUM of that column and is a scored driver, so the coarse key would have deleted real minutes from real agents. The SQL had it right; the trap is at blob level, where the timestamp field is call_dt and NOT _d.

CALLX_CALL_RECORDS.note: No natural id in the export. These four fields are unique across all 63 735 live rows, and match what row_hash would hash. Nothing to dedupe today; the key exists so an overlapping re-export cannot stack.

REFERRALS.note: Pulled from HighLevel rather than uploaded. 530 of 2 567 rows carry no contact_id at all: they cannot be keyed, so they are KEPT and counted rather than dropped — an unkeyable row is a reporting problem, not a duplicate.

session_sources._note: SES_* intraday snapshot slots take the key of the source they snapshot. Checked against the stored rows rather than the slot name: SES_DIAL_* holds CALLX-shaped rows (call_datetime, destination_number, agent), NOT ViciDial ones — keyed as ViciDial every row was unkeyable. They never mix into daily analytics, so they are deduped for size alone.
